account: Limbic Access is an AI chatbot on the websites of NHS Talking Therapies services in England that takes self-referrals for anxiety and depression and gathers information for the first assessment. Authors from Limbic, with a university co-author, analyzed data on 129,400 patients in NHS services and reported in Nature Medicine on 5 February 2024 that services using the chatbot saw referrals rise by 15%, against 6% in control services. The rise was larger for nonbinary people (179%) and for ethnic minority people (29%). The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) reviewed this and other evidence in guidance published on 24 July 2025. It states that the study showed Limbic Access to be effective at increasing referrals from people who are usually underrepresented in mental healthcare, and it allowed Limbic Access and Wysa Digital Referral Assistant in the NHS while more evidence is generated. NICE also notes that most of the evidence came from the companies or from company-affiliated authors and that evidence on time savings was limited. The study was observational, and services chose whether to adopt the chatbot.

ai_role.statement: The study compared services that adopted the chatbot with control services in routine data. Services were not randomized, so differences between services may explain part of the rise.
